body:
Omar El-Sayed: Hey folks — quick concern on SCM instrumentation. The proposed counters/timers (prefill/decode split + batch_efficiency + kv_cache_hit) look fine conceptually, but if we emit per-request w/ full tag set we’re going to pay for it in hot path. Do we have an overhead budget / can we sample?

Mateo Alvarez: +1. Runtime is already tight in decode loop. What are we actually asking to emit? aggregated counters per engine? per request? per batch?

Sofia Ivanova: From scheduling side, batch_efficiency is naturally per batch anyway. If we try to push it per request (esp w/ admission control), it gets messy + expensive.

Logan Wright: Telemetry POV: we *can* accept full-fidelity counters but not with high-cardinality tags. The draft had tags like tenant_id / route / model / region / sku / quant_profile. That’s going to explode.

Omar El-Sayed: The current draft from cost-model wants: prefill_tokens, decode_tokens, prefill_ms, decode_ms, batch_size_effective, kv_cache_hit_rate. It also wants dimensions for model_version + quant_profile_id + gpu_sku. Tenant/route are more for attribution downstream.

Nadia Rahman: Token metering is already per-request; we can join on request_id in pipeline *if* you give us a stable request_id and time window. But I agree we should not put tenant_id into runtime metrics.

Mateo Alvarez: What’s the minimum we need in runtime itself vs what can be computed later?

Logan Wright: For SCM v1, we need the *signals* to be present, but they don’t need to be emitted with every possible dimension at source. Best practice: emit low-cardinality always-on metrics (region, sku, model_family maybe), and do tenant/route attribution after the fact from logs/metering.

Thomas Baird: +1. If you emit `tenant_id` as a label we’ll be fighting fires. For high-cardinality, we should do either (a) logs with sampling or (b) span events w/ sampling. Metrics should be bounded.

Omar El-Sayed: Ok but cost-model explain endpoint wants “why was this expensive” tooltips. That’s basically per-request or per-route.

Jordan Lee: Determinism angle: SCM estimate endpoint must be deterministic given inputs. For explain/attribution, it’s ok to be “best effort” as long as assumptions/confidence reflect sampling/missingness. But we should be explicit in signals contract.

Sofia Ivanova: Suggestion: always-on aggregated counters per engine/pool:
- total_prefill_tokens, total_decode_tokens
- total_prefill_ms, total_decode_ms
- batch_size_effective_sum, batch_count
- kv_cache_hits, kv_cache_lookups
Then for explain/debug: sample per-request events at e.g. 1/128 with full context.

Mateo Alvarez: That seems reasonable. What’s sampling rate we can live with for explain? Console will get mad if every tooltip says “insufficient data”.

Logan Wright: We can do adaptive sampling: base 1/128 globally + bump to 1/16 for canary tenants / when feature flag enabled. Also we can guarantee at least N samples per (model, region, sku) per minute to keep confidence non-zero.

Nadia Rahman: If we tie the sample to request_id hashing, it’s stable and debuggable. E.g. `sample = (hash(request_id) % 128 == 0)`.

Omar El-Sayed: Implementation detail: per-request timers in decode loop are what scare me. If we only create a per-request event when sampled, we can avoid the overhead for most traffic.

Mateo Alvarez: What did we measure on a naive full-fidelity prototype?

Omar El-Sayed: I did a quick local run w/ counters on every request + tags (model, quant, sku). No tenant/route. p50 went +0.4%, p95 +1.2%. When I added per-token decode instrumentation it got ugly (+4-6%), but we don’t need per-token. Biggest cost was string label construction.

Thomas Baird: Label construction is the killer. Please keep runtime metrics labels as enums/ids (ints) if possible, or pre-interned strings.

Sofia Ivanova: For `batch_size_effective`: can compute at batch finalization (after admission control) not when request enters. Otherwise it’s wrong anyway.

Mateo Alvarez: Great call — we already had a bug there in another place.

Logan Wright: Can we align on: (1) always-on aggregated metrics, minimal label set: region, gpu_sku, model_id (or model_family), quant_profile_id. (2) sampled per-request event logs for explain, gated by config + stable hash sampling. (3) NO tenant_id / route_id labels in metrics.

Jordan Lee: And add explicit fields in the SCM contract: `attribution_source = {AGG_METRICS|SAMPLED_EVENTS|MISSING}` + `confidence_reason` includes “sampled at 1/128”.

Nadia Rahman: Works. Also: pipeline join should use request_id + tenant_id from metering events. Runtime doesn’t need tenant.

Omar El-Sayed: Cool. I’ll update runtime ticket to:
- emit aggregated counters per batch + pool
- add sampled per-request event (prefill_ms, decode_ms, kv_cache_hit bool, batch_size_effective) only when sampled
- sampling via request_id hash, default 1/128, overridable via flag

Mateo Alvarez: :thumbsup: Please drop the updated metric names in the thread when ready so we can keep them consistent w/ SCM spec.

Omar El-Sayed: Will do. Also will add a quick perf note + overhead target: <=1% p95 regression on decode-heavy workload.

Logan Wright: Sounds good. I’ll sync with Nadia/Thomas on the join + cardinality guardrails.

Sofia Ivanova: I’ll make sure batch_size_effective is computed post-admission in scheduler code path, so SCM doesn’t get nonsense.

Mateo Alvarez: Thanks all. Let’s keep the contract tight so we don’t have to rip this out later.
